chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Amr ibn Jubayr al-Azrami, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

A woman came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the husband upon the wife?' He said, 'It is more than that.' She said, 'Inform me of something from that.' He said, 'She does not fast (voluntarily) except with his permission.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a wife fasting voluntarily without her husband's permission in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'tanazzul' (yielding) in marital rights, where the husband’s permission is required for the wife’s voluntary fasting to ensure her duties to him are not neglected. Shia jurists, particularly in the Ja'fari school, distinguish this from obligatory fasting, which does not require his consent, highlighting the balance between spiritual devotion and marital obligations. The narration underscores the husband's role as the head of the household in matters of domestic harmony and resource management.
